**A POLICY THAT INCREASED CONSUMER COSTS, with differential impact by socioeconomic status.** Australia again, and again a downward access shock — rarer and more informative than an expansion, because expansions confound with secular growth in demand. Priority for the identification set.

**J. Human Resources: first-child effect on labour supply, identified off WOMEN SEEKING FERTILITY SERVICES.** Third paper in the frame using treatment-induced fertility variation for a labour question. Its first stage — how much fertility treatment actually produces — is A.17's parameter, reported as a nuisance. Route to first-stage extraction.
Sperm DNA methylation and paternal age. A.16's.

**EXPERIMENTAL evaluation of the BENEFITS AND COSTS of fertility information, including anxiety and perceived threat.** The only P6 record that treats the information intervention as having a downside. Second true experiment in the cell.
Quality-of-life instruments for infertility.

**Comparative analysis of US MANDATED BENEFIT LAWS 1949-2002.** The legislative history arm 2's treatment variable is coded from, across all mandate types — the base against which infertility mandates can be shown to be non-randomly timed.
New Zealand students' knowledge of decline via natural pregnancy AND ART — the ART-specific belief again.
OB-GYN residents' fertility knowledge.

**PRICE ELASTICITY and willingness-to-pay for fertility treatment from a discrete choice experiment.** Arm 2's structural parameter measured directly rather than inferred from a policy. If the chapter wants to translate any access change into a predicted birth response, this is the elasticity it needs.
Chinese students, Cardiff fertility knowledge scale.
Cohort study methods for subfertility. Notes population-based and clinic-based cohorts differ — a selection warning for arm 1.

**Comparative study of ART REGISTRIES themselves — coverage, definitions, completeness.** The chapter's demographic-significance arm runs entirely on registry series, so how those registries differ is a measurement-error section, not a footnote.
Antithrombotic prophylaxis in ART.
Psychological transition to parenthood after ART.
ART accessibility for people living with HIV across Europe. Companion to the HIV policy comparison in batch 8; eligibility-based access is P2's most common real-world margin.
Finnish students' knowledge of postponement's health impacts.
Scoping review of Nordic parenthood intentions and fertility knowledge, 1970-2021. THIRD review of this cell's belief side.
Histiocytosis in ART-conceived children.
Endocrine profile of infertile men.
Barriers to infertility treatment in MENA. Wall 8 — tag SECONDARY_LMIC.
Editorial on clinicians' role in Nordic fertility decline.
Heckman et al. on matching estimators. A methods record reached by citation path.
Abadie & Gardeazabal synthetic control. Same: method, not topic. Two such records now — the frame's economics seeds pull in the methods canon.
1995 NSFG summary report.
NEJM commentary on advanced maternal age.
Prediction of ongoing pregnancy after IVF. Wall 1 — but note this is the prognostic model national triage guidelines use, i.e. a rationing instrument, so its cousins may show up in P2.
No abstract. Infertility-therapy multiple pregnancies as an 'epidemic'.

Educational gradient of fertility and preferences.
'Sleepwalking into infertility' — the public-health framing of P6's mechanism as a policy problem.

**RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL of tailored fertility education.** Third RCT in P6. The cell now has a genuinely experimental belief-side literature and still nothing experimental on the behaviour side.

**Providing fertility information against INTENTIONS TO DELAY CHILDBEARING.** The closest any experiment comes to P6's actual mechanism: it manipulates the belief and measures the postponement intention. Still an intention, not a birth — but this is the record the P6 verdict will turn on.

**FIFTEEN YEARS OF AUTOLOGOUS OOCYTE THAW OUTCOMES.** With the decade-of-planned-OC record in batch 8, P5 now has two large series reporting what happens when women RETURN for their frozen eggs — the conversion rate the attitude studies cannot supply.
No abstract. One-embryo-over-two-cycles versus two-in-one: live birth AND multiple birth rates.
Duplicate of the second-unions sterility paper seen in batch 5.
Employment contracts and childbearing among Chinese academics. C.5's.
No abstract. Personality, education and time to first birth.
No abstract. 'Reproductive ageing - turning back the clock?' — the same rhetorical question P6 exists to answer.
Comparison of study designs for human fecundity. Methods.

**Journal of Economic Theory: childbearing postponement, its OPTION VALUE, and the biological clock.** P6's mechanism formalised — delay as an option whose value rises when a technology exists to exercise it later. The theoretical statement of exactly what the chapter says is empirically unmeasured.
Social background and becoming a parent, Sweden.
No abstract. Access to ART and gender equality.

**Management Science: CHAIN OWNERSHIP and fertility clinic performance.** Supply-side industrial organisation with an identification strategy. P2's cell was almost empty at the recon stage and now has clinic proximity, competition, chain ownership and eligibility rationing — thin, but a real set.
Book chapter on the experience of infertility.
